# sharqey Provider

PoC provider dla Sharqey — auth lokalna z sesji `sharqey login`, brak własnego mechanizmu logowania. Alternatively, set local_vault_path together with EXACTLY ONE of local_vault_password / local_vault_identity_key_file to operate directly on an offline `.sharqey` vault file instead of the API.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `local_vault_identity_key_file` (String) Path to an armored PGP private key file on disk — unlocks the vault at local_vault_path as one of its recipients, WITHOUT needing local_vault_password (task 067: mirrors how `sops` uses PGP keys that live in the caller's own keyring/CI secrets rather than in the encrypted file). The key must match one of the vault's recipients (see password-manager-desktop's AddRecipient) — it does not have to be the vault's own generated identity. Mutually exclusive with local_vault_password.
- `local_vault_identity_key_passphrase` (String, Sensitive) Passphrase protecting the key at local_vault_identity_key_file, if it has one (a plaintext-exported key needs none). Only valid together with local_vault_identity_key_file — this is a different secret than local_vault_password.
- `local_vault_password` (String, Sensitive) Master password for the vault's own passphrase-protected identity recipient at local_vault_path. Mutually exclusive with local_vault_identity_key_file.
- `local_vault_path` (String) Path to a local `.sharqey` vault file (format_version 4). When set (together with local_vault_password or local_vault_identity_key_file), this provider operates entirely on that file instead of the Sharqey API — no `sharqey login` session is required. Must be set together with exactly one of those two, or not at all.
- `local_vault_use_system_gpg` (Boolean) Unlock the vault at local_vault_path by shelling out to the local `gpg` binary (task 067 "Faza 3") instead of supplying a private key to this config at all — gpg-agent/pinentry own the key and its passphrase, this provider never sees either. This is the direct equivalent of how `carlpett/sops` decrypts PGP files today, and the recommended option when the vault's recipient is a real, already-unlocked personal GPG key rather than a dedicated machine key. Mutually exclusive with local_vault_password and local_vault_identity_key_file.
